planning_scheme.version: Ipswich City Plan 2025 version 2 (Amendment Package 1 - Major Amendment, s18 Tailored Process)
planning_scheme.notes: The scheme is called 'Ipswich City Plan 2025', not 'Ipswich Plan 2025'. Citation and commencement: 'This planning scheme may be cited as the Ipswich City Plan 2025.' 'The commencement date for the planning scheme was 1 July 2025.' It replaced the Ipswich Planning Scheme 2006. Appendix 2 Table AP2.1: 'Amendment Package 1 – Adopted 22 June 2026 and took effect on and from 1 July 2026.' -> 'Ipswich City Plan 2025 version 2'. The ePlan revision API (api/l/vpr) lists revisionId 203 'Version 2' (planOperative 07/01/2026, revStatus 'Current') and revisionId 199 'Version 1' (operative 07/01/2025, 'Superseded'). The revision data lists no pending plan changes (planChanges = []). Version 2 is in force as at 8 Oct 2026. The ePlan is a JavaScript-only IsoPlan app; the text was taken from the public JSON API it renders from (api/l/r/{sectionId}/0/false/30-Jun-2026/false). Human-readable ePlan links use the pattern https://ipswich.isoplan.com.au/eplan/rules/0/{sectionId}/0/0/0/203.

qdc_qhc_relationship.summary: Part 1 s1.5 Table 1.5.1 names the Dwelling House and Dual Occupancy Code (9.3.7) as the 'Alternatives to QDC boundary clearance provisions' and the 'Alternatives to QDC site cover provisions'. It names the Building Height and Density Overlay (OV6, map only, no code) as the alternative to QDC building height provisions, and the Transport and Parking Code as the alternative for car parking. s1.5(5) says all parts of QDC MP1.1 and MP1.2 apply 'unless a relevant alternative provision applies'. The code's alternative content is narrow. Front and side setbacks default back to 'Queensland Development Code MP1.1, MP1.2 or MP1.3 (as relevant)', except in (a) the New Suburban precinct (front 3m, garage door 5.5m, one-side garage built to boundary up to 9m long) and (b) the Rural zone (front 10m, side 20m). It adds a separation rule for built-to-boundary walls (900mm / 1500mm) and site cover of 60% (75% for terrace style). There is no rear setback provision, no outbuilding-specific setback/size/height rule and no pool setback rule. No reference to the Queensland Housing Code was found anywhere in the Version 2 text (keyword search of all retrieved sections). Version 2 commenced 1 July 2026, before the QHC commenced on 1 Sept 2026. Building work for a dwelling house is ADSR against this code (Table 5.7.1), so non-compliance makes the work code assessable under the planning scheme (a planning permit is needed before building approval). This is in addition to any Building Act referral.

quotes.text:
This planning scheme, through Part 5 Tables of Assessment, regulates building work in accordance with sections 32 and 33 of the Building Act 1975.
Editor's Note: The Building Act 1975 permits planning schemes to:
regulate, for the Building Code of Australia (BCA) or the Queensland Development Code (QDC), matters prescribed under a regulation under section 32 of the Building Act 1975. These include variations to provisions contained in parts MP1.1, MP1.2 and MP1.3 of the QDC such as heights of buildings related to obstruction and overshadowing, siting and design of buildings to provide visual privacy and adequate sight lines, on-site parking and outdoor living spaces etc. It may also regulate other matters, such as designating land liable to flooding, designating land as bushfire prone areas and transport noise corridors.
deal with an aspect of, or matter related or incidental to building work prescribed under a regulation under section 32 of the Building Act 1975.
specify alternative boundary clearances and site cover provisions for Class 1 and 10 structures under section 33 of the Building Act 1975.
Editor's Note: Refer to Schedule 9 of the Regulation to determine assessable development, the type of assessment and any referrals applying to the building work.

Note: For assessable building work under this planning scheme, a development permit is required.  A private certifier cannot decide a building development application under the Building Act 1975 until the planning scheme development permit is in effect.  See section 83 of the Building Act 1975 (General restrictions on granting building development approval).

definitions.text: Setback, for a building or structure, means the shortest distance, measured horizontally, between the outermost projection of the building or structure to the vertical projection of the boundary of the lot where the building or structure is.

definitions.term: setback (lower-case glossary entry - resolves to boundary clearance text)
definitions.text:
Boundary clearance means the distance between a building or structure on premises and the boundary of the premises, measured from the part of the building or structure that is closest to the boundary, other than a part that is:
an architectural or ornamental attachment; or
a rainwater fitting.
Examples:
If the fascia of a building is the part of the building that is closest to the boundary, the boundary clearance is the distance between the outside of the fascia and the boundary.
If a point on the roof of a building is the part of the building that is closest to the boundary, the boundary clearance is the distance between that point on the roof and the boundary.

Boundary clearance means the distance between a building or structure on premises and the boundary of the premises, measured from the part of the building or structure that is closest to the boundary, other than a part that is:
an architectural or ornamental attachment; or
a rainwater fitting.
Examples:
If the fascia of a building is the part of the building that is closest to the boundary, the boundary clearance is the distance between the outside of the fascia and the boundary.
If a point on the roof of a building is the part of the building that is closest to the boundary, the boundary clearance is the distance between that point on the roof and the boundary.

Building height, of a building, means:
the vertical distance, measured in metres, between the ground level of the building and the highest point on the roof of the building, other than a point that is part of an aerial, chimney, flagpole or load-bearing antenna; or
the number of storeys in the building above ground level.

Ground level means:
the level of the natural ground; or
if the level of the natural ground has changed, the level as lawfully changed.

Storey:
means a space within a building between 2 floor levels, or a floor level and a ceiling or roof, other than:a space containing only a lift shaft, stairway or meter room; or
a space containing only a bathroom, shower room, laundry, toilet or other sanitary compartment; or
a space containing only a combination of the things stated in subparagraph (i) or (ii); or
a basement with a ceiling that is not more than 1m above ground level; and
includes—a mezzanine; and
a roofed structured that is on, or part of, a rooftop, if the structure does not only accommodate building plant and equipment.

Basement means a space:
between a floor level in a building and the floor level that is immediately below it; and
no part of which is more than 1m above ground level.

Domestic outbuilding means a non-habitable class 10a building that is:
a shed, garage or carport; and
ancillary to a residential use carried out on the premises where the building is.

Dwelling house means a residential use of premises involving:
1 dwelling and any domestic outbuildings associated with the dwelling; or
2 dwellings, 1 of which is a secondary dwelling, and any domestic outbuildings associated with either dwelling.
[Examples include: Auxiliary unit]
[Examples exclude: Caretaker’s accommodation, dual occupancy, rooming accommodation, short-term accommodation, student accommodation, multiple dwelling]

Secondary dwelling means a dwelling on a lot that is used in conjunction with, but subordinate to, another dwelling on the lot, whether or not the dwelling is -
(a) attached to the other dwelling; or
(b) occupied by individuals who are related to, or associated with, the household of the other dwelling.
Domestic housing activity means the construction or use of a dwelling house and any associated buildings or structures on a lot.
Primary street frontage means, the street frontage that is most commonly addressed by other buildings in the block or as otherwise determined by the local government.

Minor building work means building work that increases the gross floor area of a building by no more than the lesser of the following:
50m2; and
an area equal to 5% of the gross floor area of the building.
Lot size is the area of a lot, excluding the are of the access handle.
Building works only means building works carried out in when the use of the building remains unchanged (so that the building works being undertaken are not associated with a material change of use).

rules.code: Dwelling House and Dual Occupancy Code
rules.clause: 9.3.7.3 Table 9.3.7.3.1 (Benchmarks for Accepted Development Subject to Requirements), RO2.1 (Table 9.3.7.3.2 AO2.1 identical)
rules.structure_scope: Dwelling house (incl. secondary dwelling) and dual occupancy. Under SC1.1 a dwelling house includes 'any domestic outbuildings associated with the dwelling', so these outcomes are read as covering associated class 10a sheds/garages/carports (not expressly stated in the RO).
rules.verbatim_text:
RO2.1
Front boundary setbacks meet the requirements of Queensland Development Code MP1.1, MP1.2 or MP1.3 (as relevant) unless:
in the New Suburban precinct, where front boundary setbacks are a minimum of 3m and 5.5m to the garage door, or
in the Rural zone, where front boundary setbacks are a minimum of 10m.

conditions: Default: comply with QDC MP1.1, MP1.2 or MP1.3 (as relevant)
exceptions: New Suburban precinct: min 3m, and 5.5m to garage door
structured.formula_text: if precinct==New Suburban: dwelling>=3m, garage door>=5.5m; elif zone==Rural: >=10m; else QDC MP1.1/MP1.2 (now QHC) value

rules.measurement_notes: SC1.2 'Setback': 'the shortest distance, measured horizontally, between the outermost projection of the building or structure to the vertical projection of the boundary of the lot'. Where the outcome defers to QDC MP1.1/MP1.2/MP1.3 the QDC measurement rules apply.
rules.notes: Part 1, s1.5 Table 1.5.1 'QDC Alternative Provisions' lists 'Alternatives to QDC boundary clearance provisions' and 'Alternatives to QDC site cover provisions' -> 'Dwelling House and Dual Occupancy Code' (and 'Alternatives to QDC building height provisions' -> 'Building Height and Density Overlay'). The table does not pin-point individual ROs/AOs; the setback/site-cover outcomes of the code are treated as the alternative provisions. The default limb cross-refers to QDC MP1.1/MP1.2/MP1.3 by their pre-QHC names; Version 2 (effective 1 July 2026) does not mention the Queensland Housing Code. How 'QDC MP1.1, MP1.2' is read after the QHC replaced them on 1 Sept 2026 needs confirmation.

local_plan_mechanism.summary: Ipswich uses 30 'Local Framework' areas (Part 4) instead of neighbourhood plans. Local Frameworks are assessment benchmarks for code and impact assessable development and rank above zone and use codes (Table 5.2.1). They are not part of the ADSR Required Outcomes for dwelling houses, so they do not change ADSR setbacks for houses or outbuildings. The DH code itself varies setbacks by precinct (New Suburban precinct of the LDR zone) and by zone (Rural). Local Frameworks mostly cross-refer to OV6 for height and to the Active Frontage Overlay for setbacks in centres. 5.3.2(9) says the Springfield Structure Plan may override the categorisation rules. Ripley Valley is a Priority Development Area with a separate development scheme (Part 10.2).

open_questions: The DH code defers front/side setbacks to 'Queensland Development Code MP1.1, MP1.2 or MP1.3', which the Queensland Housing Code replaced on 1 Sept 2026. Confirm with Council or certifiers whether these references are read as the QHC (under the Acts Interpretation Act or transitional provisions), and whether Council plans an amendment to reference the QHC.

Table 1.5.1 names the whole DH code as the alternative to QDC boundary clearance. Is that designation effective for limbs that simply say 'meet QDC MP1.1/1.2'? In substance only the New Suburban and Rural variations and RO2.3 differ from QDC.

The DH code has no rear setback provision, so rear setbacks presumably follow QDC/QHC. For the Rural zone 'side boundary setbacks ... minimum of 20m', confirm whether Council also applies it to rear boundaries and to class 10a outbuildings (no exemption is stated).
Site cover is 60% for 'Dwelling houses and Dual occupancies' regardless of lot size. QHC site cover varies by lot size; the scheme value would prevail as an alternative provision.
Building height 9.5m (RO3.2.1): Table 1.5.1 names OV6, not the DH code, as the height alternative, so it is unclear whether 9.5m operates as a QDC alternative.

No outbuilding-specific size, height or setback rule was found in the DH code or the residential zone codes. The same applies to pool setbacks, garage width relative to frontage, impervious area and landscaping (the zone codes contain only purpose and overall outcomes).

Precincts (e.g. New Suburban) are shown on the Zone and Precinct map, so a lot's precinct must be found from mapping (not extracted). OV6 heights and the Character overlay Areas A-D (Figure 8.2.3.3.20.1) are maps or images and were not extracted.

Ipswich has no 'Rural Residential' zone. The equivalents are the Large Lot and Suburban Large Lot precincts of the Low Density Residential zone (no separate DH code setbacks) and the Rural zone (10m front / 20m side).
The Table 5.7.1 preamble applies to building work that 'does not meet the definition for minor building works'. How this applies to small class 10a structures needs confirmation.

The glossary has an upper-case 'SETBACK' entry with its own definition and a lower-case 'setback' entry that resolves to the 'Boundary clearance' text. Both are quoted; which one governs is ambiguous.
